name: pixel-agents
description: A playful way to manage your AI workforce
readmeExcerpt:
🌐 Website • 🛒 VS Code • 🛒 Open VSX • 📦 npm • 👾 Discord • 🤝 Contributing • 📋 Changelog

Pixel Agents turns the AI coding agents running in your terminals into animated pixel-art characters working in a tiny office. They walk to their desks, sit down, type when they're editing files, read when they're searching, and flag you visually when they're stuck waiting for input. The office is also where you run them: launch an agent into a project, pick its character, and see how much context it has left. It ships in two forms from the same codebase: - **Standalone CLI** — `npx pixel-agents` starts a local server and serves the same office as a browser app, useful for tmux, remote, and non-VS Code workflows. - **VS Code extension** — [VS Code Marketplace](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=pablodelucca.pixel-agents) and [Open VSX](https://open-vsx.org/extension/pablodelucca/pixel-agents). Agents launch into VS Code terminals; characters render in the panel area. Claude Code is supported today; Codex, Gemini, Cursor, and others are on the roadmap. Want to add support for your favourite CLI? Join our [Discord](https://discord.gg/Yk7jXebv9H) and let us know! ## Features - **One agent, one character** — every agent terminal gets its own animated character - **Live activity tracking** — characters animate based on what the agent is actually doing (writing, reading, running commands). Sub-agents and teammates show up as their own characters - **Notifications** — speech bubbles, plus optional chimes, when an agent needs input or permission or finishes its turn - **Office layout editor** — design your office with floors, walls, furniture, and named Areas; layouts are saved across windows, export as JSON, and take external asset packs - **Your own team** — design your agents: a wardrobe of bodies, hair, clothes and accessories, colour pickers, a pixel editor, and custom items. The pixel art is based on the amazing work of [JIK-A-4, Metro City](https://jik-a-4.itch.io/metrocity-free-topdown-character-pack). - **In the browser and on your phone** — the standalone office launches agents into an embedded terminal. On a phone, via Tailscale, it can become an app with the office and the terminal a swipe apart - **Recent conversations** — past sessions listed per Directory, resumed with one click as the character they had - **Usage and context bars** — health bars for your plan limits, and one on every agent for the context it has left - **Office radio** — procedural 8-bit background music with moods and shareable song codes

## Requirements - [Claude Code CLI](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code) installed and configured - **VS Code extension:** VS Code 1.105.0 or later - **Standalone CLI:** Node.js 20 or later - Windows, Linux, or macOS ## Getting Started The VS Code extension and the standalone CLI can run side by side: both share the office layout but keep separate agents and settings. ### VS Code extension 1. Install Pixel Agents from the [VS Code Marketplace](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=pablodelucca.pixel-agents) or [Open VSX](https://open-vsx.org/extension/pablodelucca/pixel-agents). 2. Open the **Pixel Agents** panel beside the terminal. 3. Click **+** (bottom left) to open its drawer of **Directories**, then click one to launch Claude Code in it. The drawer is empty at first: turn on **Settings → Show Workspace Folders**, or add a folder with **+ Directory** (see [Directories](#directories) below). To use Claude with `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, turn on **Settings → Skip Permissions**. It stays on for every agent launched from that host until you turn it off. Only use this when you accept the security implications. Pixel Agents also detects Claude sessions started outside the extension. Turn on **Settings → Watch All Sessions** to include sessions from other workspaces. ### Standalone CLI Run Pixel Agents from anywhere: ```bash npx pixel-agents ``` The CLI prints a local URL. Click **+** to open the drawer of Directories: add one with **+ Directory**, or turn on **Settings → Show Start Directory** to list the folder you started in. Pick a Directory to launch Claude Code in the browser's embedded terminal (on a phone, tap the **+** card). Sessions started in your own terminal show up too. To install globally: ```bash npm install --global pixel-agents pixel-agents ``` Use a fixed address or port when needed: ```bash pixel-agents --port 3100 pixel-agents --host 127.0.0.1 --port 3100 pixel-agents --no-terminal pixel-agents --help ``` The printed URL carries a `?token=`. Without it you can watch the office in a sort of read-only mode: no agents can be launched, terminals are not shown, and layout and settings cannot be edited. The token is kept in `~/.pixel-agents/standalone-token`, so a bookmark keeps working if you also fix `--port`. Treat the URL as a secret: whoever holds it can do all of the above. ### On your phone, via Tailscale 1. Install [Tailscale](https://tailscale.com/download) on the computer running Pixel Agents and on your phone, both signed in to the same tailnet. 2. Start the server on a fixed port, allowing the computer's tailnet name: ```bash pixel-agents --port 3100 --allowed-host my-computer.my-tailnet.ts.net ``` 3. Serve it to your tailnet over HTTPS: ```bash tailscale serve --bg 3100 ``` 4. On your phone, open `https://my-computer.my-tailnet.ts.net/?token=…` (the `?token=` from the URL the CLI printed) and add it to the home screen. The fixed port keeps that shortcut working across restarts. Only devices on your tailnet can reach it. ## Customizing the Office ### Layout Click **Layout** to edit the office: paint floors, walls and carpets, place and recolour furniture, add pets you can click on, and paint named **Areas** that a Directory's agents prefer to sit in. Layouts can be exported and imported as JSON. ### Office assets Use **Settings → Add Asset Directory** to load external characters, pets, and furniture. See [docs/external-assets.md](docs/external-assets.md) for furniture directory structure and manifest details. The visual asset manager at `scripts/asset-manager.html` helps create furniture manifests. ### Directories A Directory is a folder you launch agents into. Click **+** to open the drawer, then **+ Directory** to add one: a name, a path (suggested from your past Claude Code sessions), and optionally the Areas its agents should sit in and the characters they wear by default. The pencil on a row you added edits or deletes it; on a phone, long-press the row. Your workspace folders (VS Code) or the directory the CLI started in (standalone) are listed too once you turn on **Settings → Show Workspace Folders** or **Show Start Directory**. ### Characters Open the roster from the arrow beside **+** and press a character's pencil (or **+ New**) to open the **Characters** view. Dress a character from the wardrobe tabs, recolour any piece, and touch up pixels in the editor; a piece you redraw can be saved as a custom item for the rest of the cast. Nothing changes in the office until you press **Save**. Characters export as a PNG or a config file, and the whole roster as a zip. Picking a character in the roster and then a Directory launches an agent as that character. In a Directory's settings you can also list its default characters, so its agents are recognisable at a glance. ## Where This Is Going The vision is to play a game and build a product. Two goals follow from it: to build a familiar, intuitive interface for running and orchestrating a lot of agents; and to make the hours you spend doing it feel less like administration and more like play. Three things get there, and they are happening in parallel, not in sequence: - **Actually a game.** Scores for whatever you care about. Furniture that _does_ things. Offices you open like save files, one per project. - **Expand the orchestration frontier.** Embedded orchestration. Form a team by dragging a box around them. Hand work between agents. Point them at a board and let them pick up tasks themselves. - **Everywhere, with everything.** Today it's Claude Code in VS Code or the browser. It should be whatever agent you run, wherever you work. A new CLI is a subdirectory, not a rewrite — this is where help is most useful right now. Most of this is still ahead. See [Issues](https://github.com/pixel-agents-hq/pixel-agents/issues) and [Discussions](https://github.com/pixel-agents-hq/pixel-agents/discussions) for what's open, and [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) to jump in. ## How It Works Pixel Agents uses two Claude Code detection paths: - **Hooks mode** (default) — a hook script receives Claude events such as `SessionStart`, `PreToolUse`, `PermissionRequest`, and `Stop`. It discovers active Pixel Agents servers and sends authenticated events to each one. - **Heuristic mode** (fallback) — when hooks are unavailable, the runtime infers agent status by scanning Claude's JSONL session transcripts under `~/.claude/projects/`. Transcripts are also read in hooks mode for details not present in an event. Pixel Agents does not modify Claude Code. Its hook configuration and persistent data live under `~/.claude/` and `~/.pixel-agents/` respectively. The usage bars are opt-in (**Settings → Usage Bars**): Claude Code reports plan limits only to its status line, so turning them on wraps your `statusLine` command in `~/.claude/settings.json` (yours keeps running unchanged), and turning them off restores it. ## Development To build from source, run the tests, or add support for another agent CLI, see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). It covers setup, the project structure, how an event reaches the office, the asset format, and the hosted test reports. The end-to-end suite is described in [e2e/README.md](e2e/README.md). ## Troubleshooting - **Standalone will not start:** verify Node.js 20+, omit `--port` to choose a free port, or select another fixed port. - **An agent is missing:** confirm **Settings → Instant Detection (Hooks)** is on and that the session belongs to the current workspace. Enable **Watch All Sessions** if needed. - **The UI looks disconnected:** open **Settings → Debug View** to inspect the server connection, transcript path, and latest agent data. - **Extension and standalone are both running:** this is supported. Current versions create separate files under `~/.pixel-agents/servers/`; stopping one does not remove the other. Still stuck? Ask in [Discord](https://discord.gg/Yk7jXebv9H) or open an [issue](https://github.com/pixel-agents-hq/pixel-agents/issues). ## Community & Contributing Join the [Discord](https://discord.gg/Yk7jXebv9H) to chat with other users and follow development. Use [Issues](https://github.com/pixel-agents-hq/pixel-agents/issues) to report bugs or request features, and [Discussions](https://github.com/pixel-agents-hq/pixel-agents/discussions) for questions and ideas. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) before opening a pull request and read our [Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) before participating. ## Supporting the Project

🌐 Website • 🛒 VS Code • 🛒 Open VSX • 📦 npm • 👾 Discord • 🤝 Contributing • 📋 Changelog

Pixel Agents turns the AI coding agents running in your terminals into animated pixel-art characters working in a tiny office. They walk to their desks, sit down, type when they're editing files, read when they're searching, and flag you visually when they're stuck waiting for input. The office is also where you run them: launch an agent into a project, pick its character, and see how much context it has left.

It ships in two forms from the same codebase:

  • Standalone CLI — npx pixel-agents starts a local server and serves the same office as a browser app, useful for tmux, remote, and non-VS Code workflows.
  • VS Code extension — VS Code Marketplace and Open VSX. Agents launch into VS Code terminals; characters render in the panel area.

Claude Code is supported today; Codex, Gemini, Cursor, and others are on the roadmap. Want to add support for your favourite CLI? Join our Discord and let us know!

Features

  • One agent, one character — every agent terminal gets its own animated character
  • Live activity tracking — characters animate based on what the agent is actually doing (writing, reading, running commands). Sub-agents and teammates show up as their own characters
  • Notifications — speech bubbles, plus optional chimes, when an agent needs input or permission or finishes its turn
  • Office layout editor — design your office with floors, walls, furniture, and named Areas; layouts are saved across windows, export as JSON, and take external asset packs
  • Your own team — design your agents: a wardrobe of bodies, hair, clothes and accessories, colour pickers, a pixel editor, and custom items. The pixel art is based on the amazing work of JIK-A-4, Metro City.
  • In the browser and on your phone — the standalone office launches agents into an embedded terminal. On a phone, via Tailscale, it can become an app with the office and the terminal a swipe apart
  • Recent conversations — past sessions listed per Directory, resumed with one click as the character they had
  • Usage and context bars — health bars for your plan limits, and one on every agent for the context it has left
  • Office radio — procedural 8-bit background music with moods and shareable song codes

Requirements

  • Claude Code CLI installed and configured
  • VS Code extension: VS Code 1.105.0 or later
  • Standalone CLI: Node.js 20 or later
  • Windows, Linux, or macOS

Getting Started

The VS Code extension and the standalone CLI can run side by side: both share the office layout but keep separate agents and settings.

VS Code extension

  1. Install Pixel Agents from the VS Code Marketplace or Open VSX.
  2. Open the Pixel Agents panel beside the terminal.
  3. Click + (bottom left) to open its drawer of Directories, then click one to launch Claude Code in it. The drawer is empty at first: turn on Settings → Show Workspace Folders, or add a folder with + Directory (see Directories below).

To use Claude with --dangerously-skip-permissions, turn on Settings → Skip Permissions. It stays on for every agent launched from that host until you turn it off. Only use this when you accept the security implications.

Pixel Agents also detects Claude sessions started outside the extension. Turn on Settings → Watch All Sessions to include sessions from other workspaces.

Standalone CLI

Run Pixel Agents from anywhere:

npx pixel-agents

The CLI prints a local URL. Click + to open the drawer of Directories: add one with + Directory, or turn on Settings → Show Start Directory to list the folder you started in. Pick a Directory to launch Claude Code in the browser's embedded terminal (on a phone, tap the + card). Sessions started in your own terminal show up too. To install globally:

npm install --global pixel-agents
pixel-agents

Use a fixed address or port when needed:

pixel-agents --port 3100
pixel-agents --host 127.0.0.1 --port 3100
pixel-agents --no-terminal
pixel-agents --help

The printed URL carries a ?token=. Without it you can watch the office in a sort of read-only mode: no agents can be launched, terminals are not shown, and layout and settings cannot be edited. The token is kept in ~/.pixel-agents/standalone-token, so a bookmark keeps working if you also fix --port. Treat the URL as a secret: whoever holds it can do all of the above.

On your phone, via Tailscale

  1. Install Tailscale on the computer running Pixel Agents and on your phone, both signed in to the same tailnet.

  2. Start the server on a fixed port, allowing the computer's tailnet name:

    pixel-agents --port 3100 --allowed-host my-computer.my-tailnet.ts.net

  3. Serve it to your tailnet over HTTPS:

    tailscale serve --bg 3100

  4. On your phone, open https://my-computer.my-tailnet.ts.net/?token=… (the ?token= from the URL the CLI printed) and add it to the home screen. The fixed port keeps that shortcut working across restarts.

Only devices on your tailnet can reach it.

Customizing the Office

Layout

Click Layout to edit the office: paint floors, walls and carpets, place and recolour furniture, add pets you can click on, and paint named Areas that a Directory's agents prefer to sit in. Layouts can be exported and imported as JSON.

Office assets

Use Settings → Add Asset Directory to load external characters, pets, and furniture. See docs/external-assets.md for furniture directory structure and manifest details. The visual asset manager at scripts/asset-manager.html helps create furniture manifests.

Directories

A Directory is a folder you launch agents into. Click + to open the drawer, then + Directory to add one: a name, a path (suggested from your past Claude Code sessions), and optionally the Areas its agents should sit in and the characters they wear by default. The pencil on a row you added edits or deletes it; on a phone, long-press the row.

Your workspace folders (VS Code) or the directory the CLI started in (standalone) are listed too once you turn on Settings → Show Workspace Folders or Show Start Directory.

Characters

Open the roster from the arrow beside + and press a character's pencil (or + New) to open the Characters view. Dress a character from the wardrobe tabs, recolour any piece, and touch up pixels in the editor; a piece you redraw can be saved as a custom item for the rest of the cast. Nothing changes in the office until you press Save. Characters export as a PNG or a config file, and the whole roster as a zip.

Picking a character in the roster and then a Directory launches an agent as that character. In a Directory's settings you can also list its default characters, so its agents are recognisable at a glance.

Where This Is Going

The vision is to play a game and build a product. Two goals follow from it: to build a familiar, intuitive interface for running and orchestrating a lot of agents; and to make the hours you spend doing it feel less like administration and more like play.

Three things get there, and they are happening in parallel, not in sequence:

  • Actually a game. Scores for whatever you care about. Furniture that does things. Offices you open like save files, one per project.
  • Expand the orchestration frontier. Embedded orchestration. Form a team by dragging a box around them. Hand work between agents. Point them at a board and let them pick up tasks themselves.
  • Everywhere, with everything. Today it's Claude Code in VS Code or the browser. It should be whatever agent you run, wherever you work. A new CLI is a subdirectory, not a rewrite — this is where help is most useful right now.

Most of this is still ahead. See Issues and Discussions for what's open, and CONTRIBUTING.md to jump in.

How It Works

Pixel Agents uses two Claude Code detection paths:

  • Hooks mode (default) — a hook script receives Claude events such as SessionStart, PreToolUse, PermissionRequest, and Stop. It discovers active Pixel Agents servers and sends authenticated events to each one.
  • Heuristic mode (fallback) — when hooks are unavailable, the runtime infers agent status by scanning Claude's JSONL session transcripts under ~/.claude/projects/. Transcripts are also read in hooks mode for details not present in an event.

Pixel Agents does not modify Claude Code. Its hook configuration and persistent data live under ~/.claude/ and ~/.pixel-agents/ respectively. The usage bars are opt-in (Settings → Usage Bars): Claude Code reports plan limits only to its status line, so turning them on wraps your statusLine command in ~/.claude/settings.json (yours keeps running unchanged), and turning them off restores it.

Development

To build from source, run the tests, or add support for another agent CLI, see CONTRIBUTING.md. It covers setup, the project structure, how an event reaches the office, the asset format, and the hosted test reports. The end-to-end suite is described in e2e/README.md.

Troubleshooting

  • Standalone will not start: verify Node.js 20+, omit --port to choose a free port, or select another fixed port.
  • An agent is missing: confirm Settings → Instant Detection (Hooks) is on and that the session belongs to the current workspace. Enable Watch All Sessions if needed.
  • The UI looks disconnected: open Settings → Debug View to inspect the server connection, transcript path, and latest agent data.
  • Extension and standalone are both running: this is supported. Current versions create separate files under ~/.pixel-agents/servers/; stopping one does not remove the other.

Still stuck? Ask in Discord or open an issue.

Community & Contributing

Join the Discord to chat with other users and follow development. Use Issues to report bugs or request features, and Discussions for questions and ideas.

See CONTRIBUTING.md before opening a pull request and read our Code of Conduct before participating.

Supporting the Project

releases.name: v1.6.0
releases.body:
### Features

- **Characters** ([#449](https://github.com/pixel-agents-hq/pixel-agents/pull/449)) — Agents are now drawn from a cast you design. The new **Characters** view dresses each character from a wardrobe (body, hair, eyes, clothes, accessories), with colour pickers and colourways, a pixel editor for touch-ups, and custom items you save from it. It edits a draft with undo and redo and an explicit **Save**, and exports a character as a PNG or a config, or the whole roster as a zip. The cast lives in `~/.pixel-agents/characters.json`, shared by VS Code and the browser.
- **Launch as a character** ([#450](https://github.com/pixel-agents-hq/pixel-agents/pull/450)) — The arrow beside **+** opens the roster: pick a character, then a Directory, and the new agent wears it. A second copy of a character gets the next clothes colour. Each Directory can also list default characters for its launches, in priority or random order.
- **Recent conversations** ([#451](https://github.com/pixel-agents-hq/pixel-agents/pull/451)) — The standalone office lists each Directory's recent Claude Code conversations, titled the way Claude Code titles them, in a left sidebar (desktop) or a slide-in menu

releases.name: v1.5.0
releases.body:
### Features

- **Embedded terminal in the browser** ([#347](https://github.com/pixel-agents-hq/pixel-agents/pull/347)) — `npx pixel-agents` is now a full surface: **+ Agent** launches Claude Code in a server-side terminal that streams into a drawer beside the office, so you can launch, watch, type into and close agents without VS Code. Terminals outlive the page, so a reload reattaches to the running session with its current screen. Pass `--no-terminal` to keep the office watch-only.
- **Mobile web app** ([#404](https://github.com/pixel-agents-hq/pixel-agents/pull/404)) — On a phone the standalone office becomes a home-screen web app: office and terminal as two pages you swipe between, a bar of agent cards, touch gestures on the office, touch scrolling and long-press selection in the terminal, and an accessory key bar above the keyboard (esc, shift+tab, paste, a trackpad key).
- **Agent cards in VS Code** ([#404](https://github.com/pixel-agents-hq/pixel-agents/pull/404)) — Every agent gets a mug shot and status dot along the office's right edge; clicking one raises its terminal and selects the character.
- **Directories** ([#405](https://github.com/pixel-agents-hq/pixel-agents/pul

releases.name: v1.4.1
releases.body:
### Features

- **Render headless agents as ghosts** ([#369](https://github.com/pixel-agents-hq/pixel-agents/pull/369)) — Agents adopted from outside the office (`claude -p`, Watch All Sessions) have no terminal to focus; a new **Display Headless as Ghosts** setting renders them translucent so they read differently from clickable agents. Off by default.

### Fixes

- **Never overwrite user settings** ([#378](https://github.com/pixel-agents-hq/pixel-agents/pull/378)) — The hook installer now aborts instead of rewriting `~/.claude/settings.json` when the file is unparseable or holds shapes it did not author, takes a one-time backup before the first write, verifies every write, and serializes consent answers. Closes [#377](https://github.com/pixel-agents-hq/pixel-agents/issues/377).
- **Sync agent state on standalone webview connect** ([#371](https://github.com/pixel-agents-hq/pixel-agents/pull/371)) — A standalone browser client that connects while agents are mid-work now receives active tool statuses, waiting status, and team metadata instead of showing every agent as idle until its next update.

releases.name: v1.4.0
releases.body:

- **Claude Code Agent Teams visualization** ([#218](https://github.com/pixel-agents-hq/pixel-agents/pull/218)) — Renders team leads and teammates as coordinated characters in both tmux and inline modes, with role labels, lead badges, token fuel gauges, tool activity, persistence, and coordinated cleanup. Builds on the early implementations in [#79](https://github.com/pixel-agents-hq/pixel-agents/pull/79) and [#177](https://github.com/pixel-agents-hq/pixel-agents/pull/177). Closes [#65](https://github.com/pixel-agents-hq/pixel-agents/issues/65).
- **Claude Code sub-agents and teammates compatible up to v2.1.220** ([#351](https://github.com/pixel-agents-hq/pixel-agents/pull/351)) — Supports the newer Claude harness, where every `Agent` spawn runs in the background against an implicit per-session team. Named spawns become seated teammate characters with their own hook routing; unnamed spawns stay Subtask sub-agents whose transcripts are watched for live tool activity. releases.name: v1.3.0
releases.body:
## Features

- **Hooks-first session management with dual-mode architecture** ([#214](https://github.com/pablodelucca/pixel-agents/pull/214)) — Splits agent detection into a preferred hooks path and a heuristic fallback. When Claude Code hooks are available, session lifecycle, tool activity, permissions, and sub-agent events are reported instantly via a local HTTP server; when unavailable, the extension transparently falls back to JSONL polling. Builds on [#187](https://github.com/pablodelucca/pixel-agents/pull/187). Closes [#188](https://github.com/pablodelucca/pixel-agents/issues/188), [#201](https://github.com/pablodelucca/pixel-agents/issues/201).
- **Claude Code hooks for instant agent status detection** ([#187](https://github.com/pablodelucca/pixel-agents/pull/187)) — Adds a standalone HTTP server and hook installer that routes 11 Claude Code hook events (SessionStart, Stop, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, SubagentStart, Notification, and others) to the webview for sub-second status updates, replacing filesystem polling when hooks are installed.
- **External session support and Agent tool recognition** ([#115](https://github.com/pablodelucca/pixel-agents/pull/115)) — Detects Claude

aiSummary.oneLiner: Visualizes your terminal AI coding agents as pixel-art characters in a tiny office.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Pixel Agents is a playful visualization tool that transforms the invisible background work of AI coding agents into an animated, visual experience. Instead of watching text scroll in a terminal, it renders a customizable 'pixel office' where animated characters represent your running agents. The characters visually reflect their current state: typing when editing code, reading when searching files, and displaying speech bubbles when stuck waiting for human input. It operates seamlessly as both a VS Code extension and a standalone local web server, adding a layer of delight and intuitive state monitoring to AI orchestration.
keyFeatures: Live state mapping: Translates terminal output and agent actions into specific character animations like typing or reading.
Dual deployment options: Runs natively as a VS Code extension panel or as a standalone local web server via the CLI.
Visual blocking alerts: Characters clearly flag the user with speech bubbles when the AI requires human intervention or approval.
Agent teams support: Orchestrates and visualizes multiple parallel agents, team leads, and ephemeral sub-agents working together.
Customizable office layouts: Users can design their virtual office, paint areas, place furniture, and load external asset packs.
Instant hook detection: Uses Claude Code hooks for sub-second status updates, falling back to transcript polling if needed.

useCases.title: Multi-agent orchestration monitoring
useCases.description: Developers running multiple AI scripts simultaneously can monitor their progress, roles, and fuel gauges visually at a glance.

useCases.title: Workflow gamification
useCases.description: Engineers add a layer of fun to long, automated refactoring tasks by watching the pixel characters walk to their desks and work.

useCases.title: Visual state interruption alerts
useCases.description: Users easily spot when an agent is blocked on an API error or needs permission just by looking at the character's animation.

useCases.title: Workspace area mapping
useCases.description: Users paint specific office zones and assign them to workspace folders, physically organizing where specific agents sit.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Developers using AI coding agents (like Claude Code) who want a more visual, intuitive, and fun way to monitor their background tasks. Users needing to work with ai-agents will find this highly applicable.
aiSummary.gettingStarted: Install via the VS Code Marketplace or run npx pixel-agents in your project directory.
